Who blocks AI bots?

NewsEcommerceCompare

A daily robots.txt audit of 1000 UK and US news publishers (811 readable today). For each one: which AI answer engines its content is open to (declared policy for the ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude search crawlers), which training bots it blocks, and its Ahrefs Domain Rating. Built for digital PR and SEO teams deciding where a placement can actually earn AI citations. Blocking a training bot is a licensing position; blocking a search bot removes you from AI answers.

421
open to all three AI answer engines
47
DR 85+ and open to all three
143
closed to all three
47
block training bots but spare GPTBot

As of 2026-08-27. 811 of 1000 tracked publishers readable. Cite as: AI Bot Blocking Tracker, Lee Foot, 2026-08-27.

How to read this
  • This is declared policy (robots.txt), not enforcement. Edge firewalls can block silently, and Open does not guarantee citations; publishers blocking search bots still get cited sometimes via retrieval from search results.
  • Open means the engine's search crawler is not blocked. Path rules means an AI-specific path restriction exists (hover the chips in the detail row for the paths). Generic sitewide housekeeping rules are treated as Open. The Training bots column is the separate licensing stance across the eight training crawlers; it does not affect whether a placement can be cited.
  • Google AI Overviews and AI Mode are not in this data. Their eligibility follows ordinary Googlebot indexing, which robots rules for AI bots do not affect. Google-Extended governs Gemini training only.

  • Fast Company: CCBot open to blocked (closed); anthropic-ai open to blocked (closed); Google-Extended open to path rules (changed); Applebot-Extended open to blocked (closed); Meta-ExternalAgent blocked to path rules (opened); Bytespider open to blocked (closed); OAI-SearchBot open to path rules (changed); Claude-SearchBot blocked to path rules (opened); ChatGPT-User open to path rules (changed); Claude-User blocked to path rules (opened); Perplexity-User blocked to path rules (opened)

Method and limits

  • One GET per domain per day to /robots.txt only, with an identifying user agent, rate limited to one request per two seconds.
  • Rules follow RFC 9309 longest-match semantics. Engine states: Blocked = Disallow: / for that engine's search crawler; Path rules = an explicit AI-specific path restriction; Open = anything else, including generic sitewide rules inherited from the * group.
  • Unreadable rows are publishers whose edge (WAF or CDN) refused even a robots.txt read from an identified audit agent. They are excluded from the headline percentages and marked Unknown.
  • Domain Rating by Ahrefs (licence), last refreshed 2026-08-12. DR moves slowly and is refreshed periodically, not daily.
  • Favicons via Google's public favicon service.
Data: news-latest.json (dated snapshots in the repo hold full history). Built by Lee Foot, ecommerce SEO consultant. More free tools at leefoot.com/tools. Domain Rating by Ahrefs.
